meta.purpose: Reviewable suggestions, not silently implemented optional trip decisions. Factual-integrity corrections are distinguished from proposals.

suggestions.title: Compare official total prices before moving the preferred dates
suggestions.body: Keep 15–22 February as the working seven-night basis. Compare eligible seven-night windows using the same named room, final fees/taxes and cancellation policy; only then consider changing dates.
suggestions.trade_off: More comparable quote research is required; the old OTA sample is not evidence that March saves money.
suggestions.evidence: Related official source observations and field gaps; this is advice, not a verified price or journey.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.title: Compare exact dates on the hotel's own booking engine before shifting the trip
previous_pass_2026_11_27.body: Do not assume 8–15 March is cheaper overall. The 25 Nov Booking.com snapshots showed lower March quotes for The Venetian, Palazzo and Cosmopolitan. On 26 Nov the Venetian's figures were not reproduced on Booking.com's own page (F-39), and the Palazzo and Cosmopolitan figures have not been re-checked (F-44). A separate official-property-engine sample reports the preferred 15–22 February week as cheapest at the properties it checked. The samples differ by property coverage, room/rate terms and fee/tax basis. This evidence does not establish a market-wide cheapest week.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.trade_off: Keeping the preferred dates avoids changing plans based on a source conflict; checking exact dates and the same room/fee basis property by property may still identify a cheaper alternative. Recheck rates close to booking because the captures are dated 25 November 2026.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.evidence: Booking.com snapshot table: data/price-windows.json and data/hotels.json. Official-engine sample with per-property booking links: docs/session-af795000/hotels.html.

suggestions.title: Keep seven- and 14-night options separate
suggestions.body: Use the seven-night draft week now. Treat 15 February–1 March as a separate possible 14-night option with its own quotes, reservations and transport checks.
suggestions.trade_off: A longer stay may change nightly rates and cancellation terms; do not double a seven-night subtotal.
suggestions.evidence: Related official source observations and field gaps; this is advice, not a verified price or journey.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.title: Decide whether this is a 3-night or a 7-night trip
previous_pass_2026_11_27.body: The brief says 1–2 weeks but the preferred dates 2027-02-15 → 2027-02-18 are three nights. Every hotel total on this site is for seven nights. If the real plan is three nights, the hotel line is roughly 43% of what is shown.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.trade_off: Three nights cannot cover 24 Michelin listings plus the museums — realistically it covers four or five restaurants. Seven nights is the shortest trip where a broad Michelin itinerary is plausible.

suggestions.title: Require a named King/Queen room rather than assigned-on-arrival inventory
suggestions.body: Attach the bed, bathroom and exact room name to the official offer. Reject an offer as verified room fit if bed allocation is left to chance.
suggestions.trade_off: The price difference is unknown until actual named-room quotes are obtained; no assumed uplift is applied.
suggestions.evidence: Related official source observations and field gaps; this is advice, not a verified price or journey.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.title: Refuse 'Room Type Assigned on Arrival' rates
previous_pass_2026_11_27.body: The three lowest Booking.com quote snapshots (LINQ $564, Flamingo $626, Horseshoe $717) are all unassigned-room promotions. These offers do not guarantee the queen-or-larger bed the couple asked for, and the quote totals are not official property rates.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.trade_off: A named king or two-queen room is necessary to verify bed fit. The price difference is not established here; check the named room on the property's official booking engine rather than adding an assumed uplift.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.evidence: data/hotels.json flags F-11 and F-29; official-engine examples are linked at docs/session-af795000/hotels.html

suggestions.title: Check restaurant availability before locking a non-refundable hotel
suggestions.body: Check the selected starred venues’ actual reservation calendars, then align flexible hotel terms with confirmed dining availability. Keep the draft week movable.
suggestions.trade_off: Availability is not established by weekly opening hours; do not reserve or pay merely to test a price.
suggestions.evidence: Related official source observations and field gaps; this is advice, not a verified price or journey.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.title: Book the four starred restaurants first, then build the trip around them
previous_pass_2026_11_27.body: é by José Andrés has nine seats and opens bookings about three months out; Joël Robuchon, L'Atelier and Guy Savoy are dinner-only and dark on specific weekdays. Reservation order should be é → Robuchon → Guy Savoy → L'Atelier, then fill the unstarred list around whatever dates remain.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.trade_off: Locking the starred nights first means the hotels must be chosen afterwards — the reverse of how people normally book.

suggestions.title: Choose transport passes only after counting real planned rides
suggestions.body: Compare RTC products with the journeys actually needed. If using optional Monorail, compare like-for-like electronic fares: 10 singles are $57.50; the seven-day pass is $59.95; 11 singles are $63.25.
suggestions.trade_off: A pass is not automatically good value and does not prove bus-only or door-to-door access.
suggestions.evidence: Related official source observations and field gaps; this is advice, not a verified price or journey.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.title: Use the Monorail 7-day pass, not single rides
previous_pass_2026_11_27.body: A single Monorail ride is $6.25 paper or $5.75 with an e-ticket; the 7-day pass is $64 paper or $59.95 electronic. Ten rides break even at paper prices. Over seven nights the pass is the cheaper and simpler option, and it covers MGM Grand ↔ SAHARA, which is exactly the Michelin corridor.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.trade_off: The Monorail does not reach Chinatown or downtown, so RTC buses are still needed for roughly half the restaurant list. The pass is not a substitute for bus fares.

suggestions.title: Test one actual bus dinner journey before trusting a cluster ranking
suggestions.body: Capture a full outward and return RTC itinerary for a shortlisted named hotel and chosen restaurant at the intended dining time. Then expand coverage systematically.
suggestions.trade_off: An in-vehicle segment alone omits walks and waiting; no assumed zone matrix should be used to fill missing journeys.
suggestions.evidence: Related official source observations and field gaps; this is advice, not a verified price or journey.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.title: Base the trip centre-Strip, not at the Venetian or the Wynn
previous_pass_2026_11_27.body: The Venetian complex holds four Michelin listings and the Wynn holds one, which makes the north Strip look like the obvious base. But the centre Strip is within 20 minutes of 15 Michelin restaurants — more than any other zone — and is reachable from both ends of the Monorail.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.trade_off: Choosing centre Strip (Cosmopolitan, ARIA, Bellagio, Vdara, Caesars) gives up the in-building convenience of four restaurants under one roof. Price comparisons should use identical dates, room classes, taxes and resort-fee basis from official property engines; the current OTA/direct samples are not comparable enough to establish a cost premium.

suggestions.title: Consider a kitchen suite only after verifying transport and total cost
suggestions.body: Desert Rose and Cliffs publish King-bed suites with kitchen facilities. They are candidates to compare, not proven lower-cost or one-hour-bus options.
suggestions.trade_off: Kitchen availability cannot compensate for an unknown journey time or unverified final room total.
suggestions.evidence: Related official source observations and field gaps; this is advice, not a verified price or journey.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.title: Pair the museums with the downtown restaurants on one day
previous_pass_2026_11_27.body: The Mob Museum, the Neon Museum, Fremont Street, Esther's Kitchen and SoulBelly BBQ are all inside the downtown/Arts District zone — which is the only zone that is far from everything else. Doing them on a single day turns a 30-minute trip each way into one trip.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.trade_off: It consumes a whole evening, so a starred dinner cannot happen that night. Slot it on arrival day.

suggestions.title: Use an itemized couple budget, not blanket fee/tax additions
suggestions.body: Keep hotel final totals, menu subtotals, activity admission, transport and optional items separate. Show unknown mandatory charges explicitly.
suggestions.trade_off: This may leave the overall trip budget blank until the official quote contains every required line.
suggestions.evidence: Related official source observations and field gaps; this is advice, not a verified price or journey.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.title: Budget resort fees and 13.38% tax explicitly
previous_pass_2026_11_27.body: The Booking.com totals this site quotes exclude the resort fee and the local room tax. On the Strip that is typically $35–$55 per night plus 13.38% — roughly $250–$390 extra on a seven-night stay, which is a whole tasting menu at Anima by EDO.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.trade_off: No downside; it is purely an accounting correction. The Wynn rows already show both bases side by side as a worked example.

suggestions.title: Keep the downtown day flexible
suggestions.body: Consider Mob Museum, Neon Museum and Fremont as a downtown group, choosing or splitting them across days. Recheck late entry and each transfer.
suggestions.trade_off: Grouping by location is not proof that all visits fit comfortably into one afternoon or that transfers take 25–30 minutes.
suggestions.evidence: Related official source observations and field gaps; this is advice, not a verified price or journey.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.title: Treat Black Friday rates as a floor, not a forecast
previous_pass_2026_11_27.body: Several of the cheapest totals captured on 2026-11-25 carry a 'Black Friday Deal' label — LINQ, Flamingo, Golden Nugget, Bluegreen, Cosmopolitan, Bellagio and Fontainebleau all show one. They expire long before 2027 and will not be reissued at the same depth.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.trade_off: Planning against the promotional number risks a 30–50% shock when the real 2027 rate appears. Use the non-promotional 'original price' figure as the conservative planning number where one is printed.

suggestions.title: Record dietary constraints before choosing a fixed tasting menu
suggestions.body: Read the chosen menu’s substitution and full-table-participation rules before selecting it as a dinner anchor.
suggestions.trade_off: Do not assume every tasting menu can accommodate an allergy or that an alternative is included at the same price.
suggestions.evidence: Related official source observations and field gaps; this is advice, not a verified price or journey.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.title: Add a 14-night column if the couple really means two weeks
previous_pass_2026_11_27.body: The brief allows 1–2 weeks. Only 7-night blocks were priced. A 14-night stay across the same date range was not measured and is flagged F-17 rather than estimated, because doubling a 7-night total would ignore weekly rate breaks.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.trade_off: Costs two more search captures per property. Worth doing only if two weeks is a real option.

suggestions.title: Add only official cross-linked social discoveries
suggestions.body: Future social additions should record exact operator cross-links or opened official-profile identity evidence, scope (venue/shared brand/parent resort), target response and capture date. PR #39 and later social research are preserved; unsupported discoveries remain separate from approved comparison fields.
suggestions.trade_off: Some cells will remain blank; a plausible handle is not enough. PR #39’s additional discoveries still need per-link reconciliation.
suggestions.evidence: Related official source observations and field gaps; this is advice, not a verified price or journey.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.title: Keep one cheap night for a jet-lagged arrival
previous_pass_2026_11_27.body: Pho Ga Bac Bac is Michelin-listed, open 24 hours, and Ping Pang Pong is open 10am–3am. Both mean the first night does not need a reservation and does not need the couple to be sharp.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.trade_off: Neither is a special-occasion room. Treat them as logistics, not as the holiday.

suggestions.title: Add a later price-refresh workflow with comparable evidence
suggestions.body: A future scheduled refresh could record official total quotes, capture dates and cancellation terms, with a review step when inventory or fee basis changes.
suggestions.trade_off: Booking engines may block automation or require interactive sessions; a failed refresh must leave values unverified, not reuse stale numbers as current.
suggestions.evidence: Related official source observations and field gaps; this is advice, not a verified price or journey.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.title: Re-verify only what can actually change
previous_pass_2026_11_27.body: Hours and days are recorded for 19 of the 24 restaurants; 5 are blank (Michael Mina, KAME, Sparrow + Wolf, Esther's Kitchen, YEN Viet) and are flagged, not guessed. 17 rows are marked verified. The four starred rooms, Michael Mina (currently marked Temporarily closed) and Wing Lei are the ones whose closure would waste an evening, so re-check those six the week before travel rather than re-checking all 24.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.trade_off: Accepts that a minor venue may be dark on the night. Saves about an hour of checking.

suggestions.title: Use field-level evidence rather than whole-row verification badges
suggestions.body: The integration now gates published fields on individual official evidence and lists nulls. Regression tests prevent model/OTA fallbacks. This factual-integrity correction is already implemented.
suggestions.trade_off: Historical datasets and archived builds retain their original limitations and are not automatically made current.
suggestions.evidence: Related official source observations and field gaps; this is advice, not a verified price or journey.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.title: Spend ten minutes closing the 28 unverified hotel links
previous_pass_2026_11_27.body: Four hotel official links were fetched and confirmed. The other 28 were written from the property's own domain but never opened, so the site labels them 'not fetched — may have moved'. That label is honest but it is also unfinished work. Opening 28 pages and fixing the dead ones would remove the caveat entirely. DONE 2026-11-26: 14 more links were opened and confirmed, the Cromwell row was renamed after its official page redirected to The Vanderpump Hotel, and the rows that refuse automated access are now labelled as refused rather than left ambiguous.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.trade_off: Ten minutes of clicking for no change to the plan's cost or ranking. The Booking.com price-source link on every card already works, so nothing is currently unreachable.

suggestions.title: Compare direct named-room alternatives on their own terms
suggestions.body: The Caesars operator page describes named King/Queen room options. A later comparison can select an eligible room explicitly rather than reuse a promotional assigned-on-arrival rate.
suggestions.trade_off: Direct, member, prepaid and refundable offers may have different conditions; do not mix them in a price ranking.
suggestions.evidence: Related official source observations and field gaps; this is advice, not a verified price or journey.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.title: Book Caesars-family rooms direct, not on the assigned-rate this site quotes
previous_pass_2026_11_27.body: The official Caesars pages for Flamingo, Horseshoe and The Vanderpump were opened on 2026-11-26 and all of them sell NAMED room types with a stated bed (e.g. Horseshoe 'Resort Executive Suite | 1 King, 650 sq ft, soaking tub'). The cheap totals on those rows come from an assigned-on-arrival OTA rate (F-11). Booking direct trades a higher nightly number for a guaranteed bed.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.trade_off: Direct is usually $100–200/week more on these three, and it removes the F-11 risk entirely.

suggestions.title: Re-quote rebranded or independently managed inventory
suggestions.body: The inherited Cromwell row now refers to The Vanderpump Hotel. Do not carry its old quote forward. For independently managed suites, establish the operator and exact terms separately from the building’s hotel page.
suggestions.trade_off: A valid building website does not prove third-party inventory identity, inclusions or a current price.
suggestions.evidence: Related official source observations and field gaps; this is advice, not a verified price or journey.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.title: Re-quote the former Cromwell row before it is used in the ranking
previous_pass_2026_11_27.body: The $1,978 seven-night total on that row was captured on 2026-11-25 under the name The Cromwell. On 2026-11-26 the property's official page presented it as The Vanderpump Hotel. Until it is re-quoted under the new brand the row is a Cromwell-era number on a Vanderpump property, and it sits at rank 7 on the Michelin-proximity table, above three cheaper centre-Strip options.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.trade_off: Costs one dated search. Until then the number should not be treated as bookable.

suggestions.title: Close the social-link gaps only from venue-controlled sources, and say where each handle came from
suggestions.body: Field-specific social provenance is implemented. Twenty restaurant Instagram profiles are approved in this pass; four remain unverified under the stricter ownership standard. Prior venue/creator video and account research is retained with the original evidence and caveats on Flagged for Review; it is not silently discarded or declared freshly rechecked.
suggestions.trade_off: Visible gaps are more honest than a plausible but unconfirmed account. Shared brand, parent-property and dormant feeds need explicit labels; no account-bio award claim overrides MICHELIN.
suggestions.evidence: F-73; data/verification.json; data/socials.json and the attributed parallel oEmbed record.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.title: Close the social-link gaps only from venue-controlled sources, and say where each handle came from
previous_pass_2026_11_27.body: The brief asked for a YouTube, TikTok or Instagram link for every restaurant and activity. YouTube is covered for all 24 restaurants and all 5 activities. The remaining gaps after the 2026-11-27 sweep are 5 restaurant Instagram handles and 22 TikTok accounts (F-53). The safe route is the venue's own site footer, its own channel/profile metadata, or its OpenTable profile — the same standard now printed under the activities table. A handle that only appears in a search result is not evidence.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.trade_off: Roughly 24 page visits plus an hour of checking, and some venues genuinely have no account — the honest outcome may be a blank cell, not a link. Filling a cell with a reseller's or creator's account would look complete and be wrong.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.evidence: F-53 ; https://neonmuseum.org/ ; https://www.youtube.com/themobmuseum ; activities page 'Where each social link came from'
